name: Peter at Antioch
charge: Dissembling: withdrawing from the Gentiles for fear of them of the circumcision
summary: At Antioch Peter had eaten with the Gentiles until certain men came from James, and then he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision, and the other Jews dissembled with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away. Paul withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed, and said before them all that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel. This history is not recorded in Acts; Paul tells it himself to the Galatians.
offenseFull: When James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace given to Paul, they gave him and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that they should go to the heathen and the pillars to the circumcision (Galatians 2:9). The heathen there is the northern kingdom, the same people called the Gentiles and the uncircumcision; the scripture itself calls the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali Galilee of the Gentiles, and those are two tribes of Israel (Matthew 4:15-16). Paul was already at Antioch doing his ministry when Peter came along later. But when Peter was come to Antioch, Paul withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed; for before certain men came from James he did eat with the Gentiles, and when they were come he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision, and the other Jews dissembled likewise with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation (Galatians 2:11-13). This history is not recorded in Acts at all. Peter was the head apostle, second in command from Christ, and he still made mistakes.

Four words carry the charge: he withdrew, he separated himself, the others dissembled, and Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation. To dissimulate is to disguise or conceal under a false appearance, to hide the real motive behind a pretense; dissimulation is feigning and hypocrisy. In plain speech, Peter was being fake, and the reason given is fear. The men he had been eating with were Israelites of the northern kingdom living in a Gentile way of life; when

the southern kingdom arrived he separated himself from them out of respect of persons, not wanting to be seen eating with them, and Barnabas withdrew with him and would not sit or eat with them either. That withdrawing is the very thing that broke the nation in the first place, when the ten tribes told Rehoboam they had no portion in David and every man went to his tent (1 Kings 12:16). The law forbids respect of persons in judgment, neither respecting the person of the poor nor honouring the person of the mighty (Leviticus 19:15). And Peter knew better than any man there, because he was the one who had been told by God not to call any man common or unclean, and the one who had watched the same gift of the Holy Ghost fall on that household (Acts 10:28, Acts 11:2-3, Acts 15:7-9).
judgmentFull: When Paul saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, he said to Peter before them all that if he, being a Jew, lived after the manner of Gentiles and not as do the Jews, he had no business compelling the Gentiles to live as do the Jews (Galatians 2:14). Paul confronted him in front of everybody. The charge was plain: you claim to be a Jew, salvation is of the Jews, you are supposed to be the example, and you are following their footsteps instead of setting one, showing respect of persons and living like them while trying to teach them to follow after the Jews. You are being a hypocrite in your actions. Paul did not let things slide; he had no respect of persons and feared no man regardless of his status. You already learned this, Peter. God showed you that you cannot call any man common or unclean. You sat with them, and you convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, and now you are wavering.

The correction went no further than the rebuke. Galatians records no sentence taking Peter out of his work, and the next words of the letter are Paul including himself with him: we who are Jews by nature, knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:15-16). Peter was corrected in front of them all and would have been embarrassed and ashamed, and he repented; and as a teacher, what does a man teach after that? What he repented from. Do not be fake. Reproof between brethren is the law and not an injury, since the commandment is to rebuke a brother plainly and not to hate him in the heart (Leviticus 19:17), and Peter himself afterward wrote of the wisdom given to our beloved brother Paul (2 Peter 3:15-16). The case is kept in the book so that a so-called Christian cannot use it to excuse breaking the commandments, and so that a man with rank among us knows that rank is no cover for hypocrisy.

lawsResolved.text: Do not be hypocritical in serving God or in living a godly life.
We are not to have hypocritical leaders because they ensnare the people.
You are not to be partial towards anyone or a respecter of persons in exacting justice, whether they be poor or rich, small or great.
If your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
We are exhorted to reprove, rebuke and correct with authority, patience and instruction.
You should not refuse to be corrected and reproved by the righteous among you.

text.text: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.
But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.
For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.
And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty: but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour.

And he said unto them, Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.

And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.
And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you;

As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.
Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.
